item.title: From Jewellery Box to Cash: What Makes Gold Earrings Valuable?
item.description: A pair of gold earrings may be worth more than they look. Value depends on purity, weight, hallmark and condition; gemstones, a designer name or antique features can add to it beyond the metal itself. How a buyer tests and prices the pair matters too, particularly if you are deciding whether to sell gold for cash or keep an unused pair in the drawer. This guide explains what affects the value of earrings, how UK hallmarking works and what to check before accepting an offer. It also looks at why one buyer’s quote can differ from another’s. Gold jewellery is made by combining gold with other metals, so two pairs that look almost identical can contain very different amounts of precious metal. The hallmark can help establish the purity of the gold. Weight is also important, although the full weight of an earring may include stones, posts, backs and other materials that are not gold. A buyer may therefore calculate the offer using the actual gold content rather than the total weight of the pair. This is where an old pair of earrings can become interesting. What may appear to be an ordinary item at the back of a jewellery box could contain a meaningful amount of gold, particularly if the earrings are heavier or made from higher-purity metal. A hallmark is one of the clearest indicators of precious-metal purity in Britain. A full UK hallmark contains a sponsor’s or maker’s mark, a fineness mark and an Assay Office mark. A date letter can also appear, although it is optional. The four UK Assay Offices are Birmingham, Edinburgh, London and Sheffield. They test precious-metal articles and apply recognised hallmarks when the required standard is met. A 2026 YouGov survey commissioned by the four UK Assay Offices found that only 52% of more than 2,000 adults were confident they understood what a hallmark meant. Once its purpose was explained, 92% said hallmarking was important when buying precious-metal jewellery. For someone assessing old earrings, the hallmark can help establish the metal standard. It does not, however, determine the resale price. Are Gold-Plated Earrings Worth the Same? No. Gold-plated jewellery has a layer of gold over another material, so it should not be valued in the same way as solid gold. UK hallmarking guidance contains specific rules for describing precious-metal articles and gold-plated silver. A gold-coloured surface does not establish that an item is solid gold. Small earrings also need extra attention. Gold articles weighing less than 1 gram are exempt from compulsory hallmarking in the UK. Check whether testing, refining, postage or other costs are deducted. Understand whether an estimate can change after inspection. Read the payment and delivery terms before sending jewellery. The advertised rate per gram is only one part of the calculation. Purity, payable weight and the buyer’s valuation method will influence the final amount. How Are Gold Earrings Tested Before Valuation? A buyer needs to know how much gold is actually in a pair of earrings before deciding what they are worth. A clear hallmark can provide useful information. But testing may be needed when the markings are worn, difficult to read or missing. The common methods for valuation are as follows: X-ray fluorescence (XRF): This is a non-destructive test that checks the metal composition without damaging the earrings. It can identify the gold content and fineness, and the Goldsmiths’ Company Assay Office says the process can take less than 30 seconds in many cases. Assay testing: Professional assay offices can test precious-metal articles to establish whether they meet the required fineness standard. This forms part of the hallmarking process used in the UK. Visual inspection: A buyer may examine hallmarks, maker’s marks, clasps, posts and other features alongside testing. This can help identify whether an item may have additional value as a finished piece. For anyone planning to sell gold for cash , testing matters because the final offer may be based on confirmed gold content rather than appearance or the stated description of the earrings. This is also why an initial estimate can change after the jewellery has been received and assessed. Which Buyer Is Right for Your Earrings? The route depends on what gives the earrings value. Damaged or incomplete earrings may mainly be worth their gold content. A complete pair with diamonds, an established maker or antique appeal may be better suited to a jewellery-focused valuation. Before deciding to sell gold for cash , identify the features that could influence the price. This can explain why two buyers may offer different amounts for the same earrings. A clear valuation should show how the figure was decided. Conclusion The value of gold earrings depends on more than their looks. The purity and weight of the gold matter most, but the brand, gemstones, design and condition can also affect the price. A hallmark can help you check the gold content. Before you decide to sell gold for cash , check your earrings properly and understand how the buyer has worked out the offer. This will help you know whether the price you are being offered is fair for the jewellery you have. item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge for Sunday’s Premier League clash against Bournemouth despite growing concern among senior club figures over the team’s performances and results. According to the BBC, Carrick is continuing as normal and has not been informed of any imminent change following United’s humiliating 4-1 defeat by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday. However, the club has begun identifying potential replacements. One source told BBC Sport: “We need to work hard to get through it.” Another acknowledged that the team’s injury problems had affected performances but insisted they were “no excuse”, describing the players’ effort levels as “concerning”. “We have a Champions League squad and need to be playing at that level,” the source added. Despite the concerns, some figures within United believe the club’s repeated changes of manager in recent years have failed to reverse its decline. They also believe Carrick has been let down by players who have failed to perform to expectations. Fernandes questions Carrick’s tactics United captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick’s tactics following Wednesday’s defeat, adding to the scrutiny surrounding the head coach. The loss to Como extended United’s winless run to seven matches in all competitions, with the club having recorded just two victories in their last 11 games. item.title: Nile University of Nigeria Inducts 75 New Medical Doctors at 5th MBBS Attestation Ceremony
item.description: Nile University of Nigeria has inducted 75 new medical doctors into the medical profession at its 5th MBBS Attestation Ceremony in Abuja, bringing the total number of doctors produced by the University since the inception of its MBBS programme to 257. The graduates, members of the University’s Class of 2025/2026, took the Physician’s Oath on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, following years of academic study and clinical training at the University’s College of Health Sciences. The ceremony marked a significant milestone for the graduates as they prepare to apply their training in professional practice. Four graduates stood out for their academic performance, recording multiple Pass with Distinction results across key medical disciplines. Abubakar Dahiru Bobo achieved seven distinctions, Shuaib Sanni Farida recorded five, while Sadi Abdu Fatima and Hafsa Awwal Abubakar each earned four. Delivering the attestation lecture, the Medical Elder, Professor Ahmed Ahidjo, former Chief Medical Director of the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital, drew on his professional experience to emphasise the importance of discipline, mentorship and continuous learning in medicine. He also discussed advances in interventional radiology and the role of innovation in medical practice, highlighting the need for doctors to keep abreast of developments in their field. The Registrar of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN), Professor Fatima Kyari, administered the Physician’s Oath and commended the University’s contribution to medical education. She urged the graduates to look beyond individual achievement and consider how they could mentor others and contribute to national development through their profession. “Start to think about today. How you will make others grow, in this profession and in the country at large,” she said. The Vice-Chancellor of Nile University of Nigeria, Prof. Dilli Dogo, FNAMed, DFMC, reminded the graduates that completing their training was the beginning of a career that would demand dedication, accountability and service. “The journey starts now. It’s a journey of service, dedication, commitment and delivery,” he said. He urged them to honour the commitments they had made in taking the Physician’s Oath, stressing the responsibility that comes with the trust placed in medical professionals. “You are called to a profession that does not tolerate excuses. I urge you to stand by the oath you’ve taken,” he added. The Vice-Chancellor also highlighted the University’s international academic links, noting that it has partnerships with 126 universities worldwide. As the graduates prepare to begin the next stage of their careers, they also received medical starter tools to support their transition into professional practice. The induction of this fifth cohort reflects Nile University of Nigeria’s continuing contribution to medical education and the development of healthcare professionals in Nigeria. item.title: ‘We were lucky to win everything’ – Messi reflects on his years at Barcelona
item.description: Barcelona legend Lionel Messi has reflected on his remarkable spell at the Spanish club, describing his time at Camp Nou as difficult to put into words. Messi returned to Spain to collect the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports at a ceremony in Oviedo, where he spoke about his memories of playing alongside some of Barcelona’s greatest stars. The Argentine, widely regarded as one of football’s greatest players, recalled sharing a dressing room with Xavi Hernandez, Andres Iniesta and Carles Puyol, highlighting the trophies they won and the enjoyment they experienced both on and off the pitch. “It was a privilege to share a dressing room with Xavi, Iniesta, Puyol and so many others. We were fortunate enough to win everything, and to do it the way we did: how much we enjoyed playing, winning and achieving great things. But above all, we enjoyed our day-to-day life, the training sessions; we had a wonderful time,” he told EFE. Reflecting further on his time at the club, Messi said his experiences in Barcelona left him with lasting memories and a special emotional connection to both the city and the team. “It is difficult to sum up in a few words. I experienced so many incredible moments and obviously hold a very, very special affection for both the city and the club.” Messi was announced as the recipient of the award earlier this year, becoming the first individual footballer to receive the honour from the Princess of Asturias Awards committee. The committee recognised not only his achievements on the pitch but also his sustained charitable efforts to improve access to education and healthcare for disadvantaged children. “In addition to his dazzling talent, his exceptional sporting career and his remarkable and sustained charitable work to promote access to education and healthcare for the most disadvantaged children,” a statement read. The award committee also praised Messi’s conduct, humility and commitment to teamwork throughout his illustrious career. “Leo Messi, the player who has won the most titles in the history of football, has also earned the respect and admiration of everyone for his exemplary behaviour on the field and for his consistency, humility and commitment to the team game.” Vanguard News The post ‘We were lucky to win everything’ – Messi reflects on his years at Barcelona appeared first on Vanguard News .

But when inflation falls, prices may still be rising, only at a slower pace. It does not mean that the cost of living has returned to what families could afford before.” Speaking further, the media chief stated, “This distinction matters for public communication. If an official says that inflation has eased, and a family hears that food is still more expensive, the family is not being unreasonable. The two statements can both be true. Good leadership explains the difference and keeps working on the effect people actually feel. “Growth must mean more than a number. It must become decent jobs, dependable public services, wages that can support a household, opportunity for young people, and confidence that the effort to build a life is worthwhile. The credibility of any economic story depends on whether citizens can find evidence of progress in their own lives.” Promoting Security Momoh also emphasised the need for intelligence, training, coordination, and public support to strengthen security agencies in the country. “Security is an even more immediate measure. Across the country, communities face insurgent violence, banditry, kidnapping, communal conflict, farmer–pastoralist tensions and other threats. In Adamawa and the wider North-East, insecurity has disrupted homes, farming, education, livelihoods and family life,” he said. “We must speak of these realities with care. Behind every statistic is a person: a child who cannot attend school, a farmer afraid to return to a field, a family forced from its home, a community unable to reach a clinic. But a good national narrative does not hide difficult truths. It gives them names, identifies responsibility, reports what is being done, and allows citizens to see whether the response is working.” On governance, he urged political leaders to match words with action for the benefit of the citizens “Every government tells a story about its purpose. It may postpone the reckoning, but it will not remove it.” “Leadership must make room for honest advice before decisions are announced. It must ask: who will benefit? Who may be harmed? How will we explain the trade-offs without talking down to the public? “The public also needs to see that leaders accept responsibility. If a project is delayed, say why and give a credible timeline. Edwin Obiorah, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), who currently occupies the position of Chancellor and Chairman of the university’s Board of Trustees. The latest development comes amid disagreements over the university’s registration, its leadership and an outstanding annual honorarium owed to Chief Rommy Ezeonwuka, who donated the institution’s take-off campus at Oba, in Idemili South Local Government Area of Anambra State. MST has reportedly terminated Obiorah’s legal representation and demanded that he hand over all files in his possession within seven days of the termination notice. In a letter jointly signed by the group’s coordinator, Rev. Dan Igwilo, and secretary, Bro. Paulde Silas Inuen, MST cited concerns over alleged conversion of institutional properties, allegedly misleading legal representations concerning the university, and what it described as the unauthorised assumption or exercise of authority in matters affecting the group. These remain allegations by the missionary group. The dispute has also extended to the appointment of the vice-chancellor. While MST reportedly wants Prof. Eugene Nwadialor retained in the position, Obiorah appointed Rev. Fr. Prof. Nnamdi Ambrose as his preferred candidate following the death of Prof. Cater Umeoduagu. Umeoduagu reportedly died about 24 hours after Obiorah appointed him acting vice-chancellor to take over from Nwadialor, who was abroad for a medical check-up. Tansian University was approved by the NUC in 2007. The ownership dispute reportedly intensified after the death of its founder, Monsignor John Bosco Akam, in 2021. Akam, a Catholic priest and founder of MSC, was said to have bequeathed the university to the missionary group in his will. NUC recognises MST In a statement dated August 18, 2026, and signed by its Director of Inspection and Monitoring, Mrs Justina Emerole, on behalf of the Executive Secretary, the NUC said it recognised MST as the proprietor of Tansian University, citing Sections 1(3) and 30 of the Tansian University Law, 2007. The commission also told the Commander of the Intelligence Response Team, Office of the Commissioner of Police, Force Intelligence Department, that it found no evidence that the names of Obiorah and members of his board had been forwarded for security clearance by the Department of State Services, as required under the relevant regulatory process. The letter, with reference number NUC/ES/15/Vol.2/449, was titled Re: Investigation Activities: Case of Criminal Conspiracy, Impersonation, Forgery, Attempted Murder and Fraud. The allegations listed in the title relate to an investigation and should not be taken as established findings against any individual. The commission said its efforts to restore peace at the university had yet to produce the desired results. “Our efforts at restoring peace in TANU over the years appears not yielding the desired fruits as evidenced by the recent crisis in the institution,” the letter stated. The NUC added that it had deployed an eight-member Forensic Audit Team to the university from June 21 to 28, 2026, to establish facts and recommend measures for resolving the dispute. It said the commission’s management was reviewing the team’s report before taking further action aimed at restoring stability and establishing a governance framework consistent with standards in Nigeria’s university system. Missionaries pledge to settle honorarium arrears Another longstanding dispute concerns the annual ₦10 million honorarium reportedly owed to Ezeonwuka for donating the property and structures used as the university’s take-off campus at Oba. According to the account provided by Ezeonwuka, an Anambra State High Court consent judgment directed the university’s management to pay him ₦10 million annually in recognition of the donation. The NUC reportedly approved the arrangement, stipulating that the payment should be described as an honorarium rather than rent for land, buildings or other property. The university paid the honorarium for some years but subsequently stopped, reportedly citing financial constraints. Ezeonwuka later obtained a judgment authorising the sale of movable and immovable university assets to recover the accumulated debt, according to the account provided. The university’s management under Obiorah challenged the judgment at the Court of Appeal. The appellate court reportedly upheld the lower court’s decision. The dispute is now before the Supreme Court, where Obiorah is challenging the decisions of the lower courts. Speaking by telephone, Ezeonwuka, who holds the title Ogilisi Igbo, said the unpaid honorarium had accumulated over more than 10 years. Rev. Val Onyelusi, a leader of MST, said the group was discussing with Ezeonwuka how to settle the outstanding amount once the missionary group regained control of the university. He said MST was prepared to honour the agreement on the annual honorarium. Onyelusi also alleged that Obiorah, who was engaged as the university’s lawyer by the late Akam, subsequently registered the institution as Tansian University Ltd/Gte and assumed the positions of chancellor and chairman of the Board of Trustees. The registration dispute remains central to the competing claims over the institution. Founder’s will cited MST also cited Akam’s will, dated October 5, 2014, which reportedly named the group as the owner of the university and the principal beneficiary of his estate. The will directed the university’s Governing Council, Board of Trustees, Pro-Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor to allocate 70 per cent of the institution’s profits to MST. The missionary group maintains that the document supports its claim to ownership and control of the university. Students caught in the dispute Meanwhile, students have reportedly been left stranded on campus amid heightened tensions, with parents seeking assurances about their children’s safety. The report said mobile policemen had barricaded the gates of both the Oba take-off campus and the main campus at Umunya. The situation has raised concerns about the disruption of academic activities and the welfare of students caught up in the ownership dispute. Efforts to obtain Obiorah’s response to MST’s termination of his legal representation and the NUC’s position on the university’s registration were unsuccessful before this report was filed. He could not be reached for comment. His response, as well as any further clarification from the university’s management, would be necessary to present the competing positions fully. item.title: USA to host first women’s football Club World Cup in 2028 – FIFA
item.description: The United States will host the inaugural women’s football Club World Cup in 2028, FIFA announced Thursday. “The decision was taken in view of its experience in organising FIFA tournaments, the maturity of its infrastructure and services and the level of stakeholder interest in women’s football in the country,” world football’s governing body said. The competition will be staged from January 5-30, 2028. It will bring together 16 top-tier clubs from all six continental confederations. FIFA said the introduction of the tournament marked “a major milestone for the professionalisation and global expansion of the women’s club game, giving elite club sides a true world stage to compete on every four years”. Initially slated for 2026, FIFA pushed the inaugural tournament back by two years so it enjoys a clear window following the 2027 women’s World Cup and ahead of the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles. The US has a proven track record of hosting large sporting events, notably staging the men’s World Cup earlier this year. Nigerians travelling with local delicacies should check the ingredients carefully before packing them. The UK government’s guidance on bringing meat, dairy, fish and other animal products into Great Britain explains the applicable restrictions and exceptions. 5. Milk and dairy products Milk, cheese, butter, yoghurt and other dairy products are subject to restrictions when brought into Great Britain from abroad. For travellers arriving from Nigeria, milk and milk-based products are generally prohibited, although exceptions exist for certain products, including specified infant formula and special foods required for medical reasons. The rules include conditions on quantities and packaging for eligible exceptions. Travellers should check the latest requirements before carrying powdered milk, cheese, butter or other dairy products in their luggage. 6. Endangered animal and plant products Items made from endangered animals or plants may be prohibited or require special permits and certificates before they can enter the UK. These can include ivory ornaments, certain animal skins, exotic leather products, protected coral, rare plants and souvenirs made from endangered species. Some products may appear to be ordinary gifts or decorative items but still fall under international wildlife-trade restrictions. item.title: South-West: Why I’m contesting against Tinubu – Makinde
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Seyi Makinde, Oyo State governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), has defended his decision to contest the 2027 presidential election, insisting that the South-West can field two candidates. His position comes as President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking re-election for a second term on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), is from the same region. The governor spoke on Thursday in Akure, the Ondo State capital, at the APM Makinde/Daura Campaign Organisation’s South-West town hall meeting. Defending his decision, Makinde cited the 1999 election, when former President Olusegun Obasanjo and the late Olu Falae, both from the South-West, contested the presidency. “The southwest zone of Nigeria has always been in the forefront of a better country for us. I’ve listened to people; they said to us, ‘Seyi Makinde, why are you contesting in this election when the southwest already has somebody seated on that seat?’ “I explained to them, ‘We do have an example here in the southwest when, in 1999, the entire Nigeria ceased the presidency to the southwest, and we had two of our fathers, Baba President Obasnajo and Baba Olu Falae; they contested the presidency both from the same region, and heaven did not fall “As a matter of fact, what the Southwest did was to present two of their finest and best for Nigeria to choose from. Is there anything wrong with that this time around?” he asked. The governor urged the region to reject what he described as the “politics of deceit”, saying his administration’s record in Oyo State offered examples of what he could deliver. Makinde questioned the decision of Nigeria’s permanent representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, to present the UN budget to President Tinubu, arguing that the expenditure was unjustified amid uncertainty over Nigeria’s own budget implementation. “I was watching on TV two days ago; Nigeria’s permanent representative at the United Nations brought the budget of the UN to present to the president of Nigeria in Nigeria. They can waste the taxpayers’ money because I refuse to agree that you must use the taxpayers’ money to fly from New York to Abuja to present the UN budget when, in fact, this is an administration that right now we don’t know which budget we’re operating on for Nigeria. “Is it the 2023, 2024, 2025 or 2026 budget? And then they’re coming with the UN budget to say this is it.” He contrasted the situation with his administration’s record in Oyo State, saying budget performance had improved from between 28 and 30 per cent when he assumed office to more than 70 per cent over the past seven years. Makinde said the improvement was sustained annually and added that his administration had operated a budget cycle running from January to December. item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has yet to declare whether it will support or oppose Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president, leaving Asia’s 47 member associations potentially decisive in the March 2027 contest. According to ESPN, AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa gave no clear indication of the continental body’s position while addressing the close of a two-day meeting in Tokyo on Thursday. The Asian bloc could prove influential in the election, with Infantino facing opposition in Europe, strong backing in Africa and uncertainty over how Asian members will vote. “For people who try to divide us this is not going to happen,” Sheikh Salman said, insisting the organisation would act in the best interests of football rather than align itself with any individual. “We’re not against anyone and we’re not in favour of anyone. We’re always going to express our feelings and try to do what’s best and what’s right for football. Not just in Asia,” he added. The position marks a shift from just over two months ago, when the Asian confederation joined football governing bodies in Europe, North and Central America in accusing Infantino of a “fundamental breach of trust”. However, Asia remains divided over the FIFA president’s leadership, with Qatar, host of the 2022 World Cup, backing him, while Jordan has declared its opposition. Infantino is seeking a fourth term as FIFA president, with prospective challengers required to submit their nominations by November 18. No opponent had emerged at the time of the report. The FIFA president has also faced criticism over a now-abandoned $4.2 billion proposal to transfer part of FIFA’s World Cup commercial rights to a private investment firm. Infantino apologised to FIFA’s 37-member Council in Zurich last week for mistakes made in handling the proposal, which drew calls for greater transparency. An Associated Press tally cited in the report indicated that 87 of FIFA’s 211 member associations had expressed support for Infantino, either individually or through statements issued by their regional confederations. Meanwhile, Sheikh Salman acknowledged that political and economic developments, particularly tensions in the Middle East, continued to affect football across the region. The Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia is scheduled to be held from January 7 to February 5, with 24 teams expected to compete in Riyadh, Jeddah and Khobar despite security concerns linked to regional hostilities. Tournament organisers said they were monitoring developments and working with the AFC to ensure the competition could proceed as planned. item.title: Mourinho, Mbappe defend Vinicius after Madrid fans boo Brazilian in Leipzig win
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Real Madrid coach José Mourinho and forward Kylian Mbappé have defended Vinicius Júnior after the Brazilian was booed by home supporters during their 4-1 victory over RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday. According to ESPN, Vinícius was substituted in the 70th minute of Wednesday’s match at the Santiago Bernabéu, having gone nine consecutive games without scoring for Los Blancos. Mourinho acknowledged the emotional impact of being booed by one’s own supporters, contrasting it with the motivation players sometimes draw from criticism by opposing fans. “When you are on the pitch and you are whistled when playing away, often it’s a boost to your motivation. When it’s at home, it hurts,” Mourinho said. Despite the criticism, the Portuguese coach praised Vinícius’ contribution to the team, highlighting his defensive work and overall performance. “Only he can say whether he feels sad, but I am pleased,” Mourinho said. “Vini put in a good tactical performance. Vini defended very well. He then had a chance to score a brilliant goal, but the goalkeeper made a great save.” Vinicius has managed just one goal and three assists in 11 appearances this season. He also missed the weekend’s LaLiga fixture while serving the first match of a four-game suspension. Mourinho also urged the Brazilian to remain focused on improving his fitness and form during the period he will be unavailable for domestic league action. “Work, work. He cannot play but he can work his physique with an individualised plan,” he said, adding that he was satisfied with the forward’s performance against Leipzig despite his failure to score. Mbappé, who was named player of the match after providing an assist for Madrid’s second goal and scoring their third, also backed his teammate to rediscover his best form. The French forward said Vinícius’ frustration reflected his desire to contribute more to the team and satisfy the club’s supporters. “He’s doing well. It’s good that he’s upset because it means he wants to give a lot to the team and the fans,” Mbappé said. “I think he just needs to stay calm and proud of who he is. A great player must always take pride in who they are and gain confidence because the quality is there.” Vinícius, meanwhile, appeared to respond to the criticism in a social media post after the match, writing: “Living in the moment. Everything passes,” alongside a winking emoji. The post Mourinho, Mbappe defend Vinicius after Madrid fans boo Brazilian in Leipzig win appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: France records first human death linked to Shamonda virus
item.description: — Authorities say patient was severely immunocompromised, no public health risk identified France has reported the death of a severely immunocompromised patient infected with Shamonda virus, marking the first recorded human case of the virus. The death was announced on Thursday in a statement by the French ministries responsible for health and agriculture, according to Agence France-Presse (AFP). The ministries described the infection as “an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient”. The patient, who died in early October, was believed to have contracted the virus through the bite of a midge in eastern France, where the virus had been circulating among animals during the spring and summer. French authorities said clinical, biological and epidemiological investigations were ongoing, adding that no risk to the general public had been identified at the time of the announcement. “Despite circulating in Africa and Asia for several decades, the Shamonda virus has never previously been detected in humans,” the statement said. It added that the neurological complications observed in the patient before his death were very likely linked to the infection. About Shamonda virus According to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Shamonda virus is a vector-borne pathogen belonging to the Orthobunyavirus group. It is transmitted to animals by small biting insects. The virus was first isolated from cattle in Nigeria in 1965 and was subsequently identified in other parts of Africa and Asia in the early 2000s. In Europe, clinical signs of the virus in animals were reported from June 2026 and identified in late July, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). The ECDC said the virus had been detected in farm animals in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain and Switzerland, as well as Jersey. The agency said it was working with French authorities and European partners to investigate the potential public health implications of the first reported human infection. Kaseya made the appeal during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief, saying the woman had travelled to Uganda, where she spent several days before her husband joined her. He said the couple returned to Abuja on October 3, adding that authorities were investigating whether she contracted the virus in Uganda or another location. The Federal Government confirmed Nigeria’s first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease on October 20, after laboratory tests detected the virus in a woman who had recently arrived in the country. item.title: Ebola: ‘They’ll Be Blacklisted,’ Africa CDC Warns Aid Partners Against Lack Of Transparency
item.description: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has warned that it will blacklist partners who fail to account for funds received to combat disease outbreaks on the continent. ﻿ It also warned that the era of organisations operating without transparency is over. He expressed displeasure that, out of the $962 million already disbursed from the $3 billion pledge made on the margins of the UN, the G20 meeting in September, some partners claimed they received around $220 million. “There was a practice in many African countries, I say many, not all, but many. Partners will get money from donors. They will implement their activities without disclosing how much they got, without even sending a report to the government,” Kaseya. “And when the outbreak is over, we’ll hear from some capitals that billions of dollars were invested to stop this outbreak. I said, enough is enough. It will never happen again on this continent. “We managed to fundraise. We got figures from all donors. Out of $3 billion pledged, based on the last meeting that the US organised in September on the margins of the UN G20 meeting, we got a total pledge of $3 billion.” “Out of that, $962 million was already disbursed. We went to work with the DRC government. We organised a meeting with partners. Only 19 out of 92 partners attended. item.title: [VIDEO] Why Vaccines Aren’t Available For Latest Ebola Outbreak — Africa CDC
item.description: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has explained why the continent has yet to find a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola disease. Speaking during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, the Director General of the Africa CDC, Dr. Jean Kaseya, said some partners consider Ebola an African issue, adding that “if this outbreak was in Western countries, vaccines would already be available”. He, however, said that the agency had initiated clinical trials of new vaccines, including a new Bundibugyo vaccine manufactured in Egypt.
